E. PLANNED CHANGES TO IMPROVE SAFETY

The Louisville-Algonquin LP Terminal is continually striving to make itself the safest and most reliable workplace possible for its employees, neighbors and the surrounding community.  The Terminal looks for and actively seeks employee input regarding process safety and improvement in accordance with corporate Employee Participation Program.  All Process Safety Events (as defined in API 754) are electronically recorded, reviewed, and investigated up to utilizing Root Cause methodologies (ex. TapRooT.)

ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION AND EMERGENCY RELEASE POLICIES

The MPLX Louisville-Algonquin Parkway LP Terminal is a refined petroleum storage and distribution facility providing product throughout the region.  The RMP-regulated process (stationary source) is limited to the on-site Butane Blending system which allows for the fuel blending of n-Butane into on-site gasoline streams.  The process includes one pressure vessel, a transport offload station, pump, piping and associated appurtenances. 

The Louisville-Algonquin LP Terminal is committed to operating and maintaining processes in a safe, reliable and environmentally sound manner. The Terminal believes that excellent performance in health, safety, and the environment goes hand in hand with operating reliably, and that outstanding health, safety, and environmental (HES ) performance is of paramount importance.

Site processes are designed, operated and maintained in a manner that protects the environment, as well as the health and safety of its employees, contractors and the community. The Terminal promotes health, safety, and the environment through programs of awareness, compliance, prevention and protection. These programs include a combination of accidental release prevention and emergency response planning. This document provides a brief overview of the comprehensive risk management activities that the facility has designed and implemented, including:

A. A description of the facility and the use of regulated substance (n-Butane);
B. An overview of the accidental release prevention programs (Program Level 3);
C. A five-year accident history for accidental releases of regulated chemicals;
D. An overview of the emergency response program; and
E. An overview of planned changes to improve safety.

A. STATIONARY SOURCE AND REGULATED SUBSTANCES

The Butane Blending process has been classified as Program Level 3. No Program 1 or 2 processes are identified. By virtue of the flammable effects associated with Butane,

it is necessary to observe certain safety precautions while handling Butane to prevent unnecessary human exposure, to reduce the threat to employee health, and to minimize potential impacts to nearby members of the community.  Safety at the Terminal depends upon the manner in which Butane is handled as well as the various safety/control devices incorporated into the design of the process. Furthermore, comprehensive training is provided to employees, which reinforces the safety policies and procedures of the Terminal.

The Facility has fixed inventories of butane. Butane is received by truck (transports) and stored in one (1) storage pressure vessel.  The butane is pumped to an injection skid for direct injection into various unleaded gasoline streams. Injection quantities are controlled via the injection skid, gasoline analyzer and PLC.  Process safety controls include excess flow valves, low-melting point (<250 degrees Fahrenheit) fusible elements, fail safe valves, vessel high-level shutoffs, emergency shutoff devices on the system and video display terminal, thermal/pressure reliefs, and grounding/interlock devices. Access to the Louisville-Algonquin LP Terminal is restricted to authorized employees, management personnel and approved contractors/visitors.

B. GENERAL ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM AND CHEMICAL-SPECIFIC
PREVENTION MEASURES

The MPLX Louisville-Algonquin LP Terminal's accidental release prevention programs and emergency planning and response programs help effectively manage the hazards posed to employees, the public, and the environment by on-site hazardous substances . The covered process is regulated by the EPA RMP Rule (40 CFR Part 68) as well as the OSHA Process Safety Management standard (29CFR 1910.119.) The following accident prevention program elements are in place at the Terminal:

1) Employee Participation,
2) Process Safety Information,
3) Process Hazard Analyses (PHAs,)
4) Standard Operating Procedures,
5) Operator and Maintenan

ce Training,
6) Contractor Management and Evaluations,
7) Pre-startup Safety Review,
8) Mechanical Integrity with Performance Testing/Preventive Maintenance,
9) Safe Work Permits
10) Management of Change
11) Incident and Process Safety  Event Investigation,
12) Emergency Planning and Response,
13) Internal and Regulatory Compliance Audits, and 
14) Trade Secrets.

These fourteen (14) individual elements of the prevention program work together to prevent and mitigate accidental chemical releases.  The Louisville-Algonquin LP Terminal and its employees are committed to the standards required by these management programs. In addition to the above elements, there are also specific prevention measures that are employed as part of the Terminal's operating procedures and engineering/administrative controls to help contain/control, quickly detect and reduce the consequences of a release. These are briefly summarized as follows:

General Risk Reduction and Safety Measures

-Engineering and construction in accordance with recognized industry (ex. NPFA 58) and company standards,
-Equipment properly designed with protection from overpressure (pressure safety relief valves, etc.),
-Updated technical drawings, Piping & Instrument Diagrams and Process Flow Diagrams,
-Operating systems monitored and controlled by trained personnel, 
-Computerized monitoring (local and remote) with control of process operations,
-Redundant safety systems with emergency power,
-Automatic and manual shutdown devices for critical systems,
-Scheduled inspection and testing of instruments, Butane-containing components, and safety devices,
-Controlled/secured facility access,
-Regular safety meetings and safety awareness programs,
-Routinely scheduled safety inspections and audits, and
-Frequent process surveillance by operators.

General Release Mitigation

-Automatic and remotely operated shut-offs to limit release quantity,
-Strategically located valves to isolate leaks,
-Hydrocarbon detectors at key a

reas to warn of a chemical release and disable the process, and
-Dry-line cooling monitors installed near the butane storage vessels. 

General Emergency Response

-Emergency alert system,
-Periodic emergency training for employees,
-Communication systems with local emergency responders and regulatory agencies,
-Emergency drills with site personnel, regulatory agencies, and community emergency responders to enhance response skills and coordination among agencies,
-Mutual Aid with Local Fire Departments, and
-Participation with the local LEPC/EMAs.

The Butane Blending process was designed and constructed per National Fire Protection Association's (NFPA's) Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) Code (NFPA-58) requirements for LP Gas storage. In addition to the presence of appropriate controls to prevent possible releases of Butane, if a release does occur, emergency response and action plans ("Smart Plan") are in place with response activities being coordinated with the Pleasure Ridge Park (PRP) Fire District, Louisville Fire Department and Louisville Metro Emergency Management.

C. FIVE YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY

The Louisville-Algonquin LP Terminal has an excellent record of accident prevention. The Terminal maintains records for all  accidental chemical releases that occur at its facility.  As this is a newly regulated process, there have been no reportable accidents within the past five (5) years resulting from the release of materials covered under the EPA RMP regulation.

D. EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM

The Louisville-Algonquin LP Terminal is identified as a Non-Responding Stationary Source and, as such, utilizes outside sources (i.e. municipal fire departments) for offensive-type responses.
